title: Note on proliferation transitions of non-Abelian anyons
abstract: We study phase transitions out of a (2+1)d topological phase driven by the proliferation of anyons in a braided fusion subcategory. We describe a general theoretical framework for such transitions, in which the topological quantum field theory (TQFT) is coupled to dynamical matter associated with anyons in the subcategory. We interpret this construction using symmetry topological field theory (SymTFT), where the dynamics is localized on the symmetry boundary of the (3+1)d slab. We analyze several examples, and present explicit Chern-Simons-Higgs (CSH) field theories realizing the proliferation transitions. We also examine proliferation transitions that implement gauging of non-invertible one-form symmetry in the parent TQFT. This includes a general construction for ${\rm Rep}(G)$ one-form symmetry for a finite group $G$, and a CSH realization of the non-invertible one-form gauging ${\rm SU}(2)_{10}\rightarrow {\rm Spin}(5)_1$. We discuss which anyons proliferate at these transitions.
summary: This work develops a general theoretical framework to describe phase transitions in topological phases driven by the proliferation of non-Abelian anyons. It utilizes Symmetry Topological Field Theory (SymTFT) to model these transitions, showing they can be explicitly realized by Chern-Simons-Higgs theories. This provides a powerful mathematical tool for classifying and understanding exotic quantum phases in condensed matter systems.
main_problem: The paper studies phase transitions occurring when non-Abelian anyons proliferate within a $(2+1)$d topological phase.
main_result: It establishes a general theoretical framework using Symmetry Topological Field Theory (SymTFT) and demonstrates that these transitions can be realized by Chern-Simons-Higgs (CSH) field theories.
method: The analysis employs advanced field theory techniques, including SymTFT, the study of braided fusion subcategories, and the analysis of Higgs mechanisms in gauge theories.
model_or_system: The system involves a Topological Quantum Field Theory (TQFT) coupled to dynamical matter associated with non-Abelian anyons. Specific models analyzed include CSH theories and the gauging of non-invertible one-form symmetries.
key_observables: The type of anyons that proliferate, the resulting low-energy effective TQFT, and the structure of the Higgs potential.
important_parameters: The structure of the braided fusion subcategory ($B$), the coupling constants in the CSH Lagrangian (e.g., $r, \lambda, \kappa$), and the symmetry group $G$.
main_assumptions: The framework relies on the SymTFT interpretation, and some mathematical identities are established for specific cases rather than being fully general.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the general framework for anyon proliferation transitions using SymTFT, to analyzing specific realizations via CSH theories, and concluding with detailed examples involving the gauging of non-invertible symmetries.
why_interesting: The deep connection between topological order, symmetry protection, and effective field theories (like CSH) provides powerful mathematical tools applicable to understanding emergent phenomena in strongly correlated electron systems.
